writtenNote: Not written first. The task asked for this plan before execution; it was written at 15:30Z, after the three CI dispatches of 15:06Z (recorded in ledger.json) and after the first local runs (Z3 bootstrap, locked restore, build, B1 regeneration, the B2 gate, two packs, two website builds, the fresh-clone run). The commands below are the ones those runs used, taken from the inventory and the workflows; no command was chosen after seeing a result. Deviations are recorded in ledger.json deviations.
rules: Every output is produced from the candidate commit: local runs from a detached checkout of the candidate (the C2 agent worktree, `git checkout --detach 696ab824...`) and from a fresh clone checked out at the candidate; CI runs only by workflow_dispatch on the temporary branch c2-1424/candidate-696ab824, which points exactly at the candidate, and each run's head_sha is verified equal to the candidate.

Nothing is published: no package push, no tag, no GitHub release, no release-asset upload, no Pages deploy, no publication PR, no commit to main (contract section 7 releasePath.publicationSeparation). publish-nuget.yml, nextjs-gh-pages.yml, benchmark.yml, and verify-release.yml are never dispatched.

Every attempt is retained in ledger.json, including infrastructure failures. Nothing is re-run until green, and GitHub's job re-run is never used. A lane is dispatched again (a new run, whole workflow) only when jobs of its previous run never started because GitHub could not acquire a runner ('The job was not started because it repeatedly failed to be acquired'; githubstatus Actions major_outage 15:14Z-15:32Z), and at most once per lane; both runs are recorded and neither replaces the other. This rule was written after observing that infrastructure failure in the 15:06Z runs.

The determinism protocol is not dispatched again by C2 without a maintainer decision: its registered case registry no longer matches the candidate (ledger.json blocked row DETERMINISM-REGISTRY-DRIFT), so an execution could not be DETERMINISTIC and would use the protocol's last execution slot (maxExecutions 3).

Historical-only artifacts are not regenerated. Stale artifacts keep their frozen classification: where a repaired producer exists, its output is regenerated and recorded as a candidate output, and the row says the inventory still classifies the artifact stale.
Every output lands under docs/plans/evidence/c2-1424/ as newly added .json/.jsonl/.md/.txt/.log/.trx/.csv/.gz/.sha256 files, the only paths C1's invalidation classifier exempts after the landing.
